title: 2026-10-31_Ransomware_Incident_Response_Scenario_705
description: Investigate a ransomware incident, identify the threat, and contain the damage on a compromised Linux system.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The victim host in your network has been compromised by ransomware. Your task is to investigate the incident, identify the threat, and contain the damage. The victim host is running a Linux operating system and has been exhibiting unusual network activity. Your goal is to understand the scope of the compromise, identify the command and control infrastructure, and prevent further data exfiltration.

levels.title: Identify the external host communicating with the compromised system
levels.content: Analyze network connections and identify the ransomware command-and-control server.
levels.solution:
1. Check active network connections using the command: `netstat -tuln`.
2. Look for suspicious outbound connections, particularly those to external IP addresses.
3. Use the command `ss -tulnp` to get more detailed information about the connections.

levels.title: Determine which network port is used for suspicious command-and-control communication
levels.content: Investigate network traffic to identify ports used by the ransomware.
levels.solution:
1. Use the command `netstat -tuln` to list all active connections and their ports.
2. Look for unusual ports that are open and being used for outbound connections.
3. Use the command `ss -tulnp` to get more detailed information about the ports and processes using them.

levels.title: Identify the external host receiving sensitive data from the compromised system
levels.content: Analyze outbound network traffic to identify the exfiltration infrastructure.
levels.solution:
1. Use the command `netstat -tuln` to list all active connections.
2. Look for connections to external IP addresses that indicate data exfiltration.
3. Use the command `ss -tulnp` to get more detailed information about the connections and the processes involved.
